Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Don Little accuses female police officer of verbal abuse during encounter in Kumasi Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 17 November 2026 11:23am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ghanaian actor Don Little has expressed anger and disappointment towards an unnamed female officer of the Ghana Police Service following an alleged unpleasant encounter with a female police officer at Kumasi Breman.
In a viral video shared on X on November 17, 2026, the actor recounted how the officer allegedly stopped his vehicle and verbally assaulted him during a confrontation.
According to Don Little, the incident began when he failed to notice a torchlight the officer had flashed towards him. He claimed that the officer became upset and started hitting his vehicle, prompting him to question her conduct.
Narrating his experience, the actor criticised the behaviour of some police officers, insisting that those entrusted with maintaining law and order should treat members of the public with respect.
Don Little further alleged that the confrontation escalated when the female officer made a derogatory remark about his height, reportedly comparing it to the size of her clitoris.
Some people are mean o eiii. how can you look at Don Little and tell him your clit is longer than him? 🤦‍♂so mean. Kafra Don. https://t.co/kdoHd80tHY
He disclosed that the comment deeply offended him, describing the officer's alleged behaviour as unacceptable and disrespectful.
The actor also issued a strong warning to the Ghana Police Service, cautioning that he would not tolerate a similar incident in the future. He threatened to take drastic action should another officer mistreat him without justification.
In his remarks, Don Little questioned the professionalism of the officer involved and called attention to what he considers inappropriate conduct by some members of the police service.
The allegations have drawn attention to the importance of professionalism, respectful communication and accountability in interactions between police officers and civilians.
